POST /push/progress
  A workflow says it is running, in a node. A run groom has not seen joins the fleet; one it has seen is running again and keeps its gates. A field the push leaves out stays as it was.
  auth: none
  body: Progress
  201 → Ack: {ok: true}: groom took the push and the run is on the fleet running; a new run is named by its name or else its container id
  400 → Error: the body is not JSON, or is not an object
  carries: PushProgress
source: groom/groom/app.py::push_progress
source: groom/groom/state.py::upsert_workflow

POST /push/blocked
  A workflow says it waits on the operator at a gate file. The run is blocked and holds one gate per file path; a second push for the same path replaces its question. It needs both a container id and a file path.
  auth: none
  body: Blocked
  201 → Ack: {ok: true}: groom took the push and the run is on the fleet blocked on the gate file
  400 → Error: the body is not JSON, or is not an object
  500 → ServerError: a name that is not text cannot be ordered against the name of another run in the same state
    why: groom sorts the fleet by rank and name
  carries: PushBlocked
source: groom/groom/app.py::push_blocked
source: groom/groom/state.py::upsert_workflow

POST /push/exited
  A workflow's process ended. The run is finished and holds no gates. An exit code that is absent or not a number leaves the run's earlier code as it was.
  auth: none
  body: Exited
  201 → Ack: {ok: true}: groom took the push and the run is on the fleet finished; its gates are gone
  400 → Error: the body is not JSON, or is not an object
  500 → ServerError: a name that is not text cannot be ordered against the name of another run in the same state
    why: groom sorts the fleet by rank and name
  carries: PushExited

GET /api/state
  Reads the fleet. Runs come blocked first, then running, then finished, each group by name. The attention list covers every run and ignores q.
  auth: none
  query:
    q  id of Run (string) — keeps the runs where this text, in any case, is part of the name, repo, branch, node, run id or a gate path
    not compared at 200 ts: the server's clock
    not compared at 200 v: counts the fleet frames the server has sent since it started
    not compared at 200 scanning: a discovery scan may be running
    not compared at 200 runs[].row_id: the first four characters of the container id, which carries the minted suffix
    not compared at 200 runs[].last_seen_ts: the moment of the run's last signal, which the clock decides
    not compared at 200 status: counts every run of the environment
    not compared at 200 store: the state of the environment's database
    not compared at 200 attend.by_run: the attendant's jobs belong to the whole environment
    not compared at 200 attend.rev: counts every change the attendant has seen
    not compared at 200 attend.count: counts the jobs of the whole environment
  200 → Fleet: the fleet as the dashboard shows it, filtered by q
  carries: ReadFleet

GET /api/run/{run_id}/records
  Reads one page of a run's stored records, newest first, from the cursor a previous page returned.
  auth: none
  path:
    run_id  id of Run (string) (required) — the run's id, as the dashboard addresses it
  query:
    before   string — the cursor the previous page returned
    limit    integer — how many records a page holds; a value under 1 holds none
    metrics  integer — 1 adds the metric samples
  200 → Records: one page of the run's stored records, newest first
  400 → Error: the cursor is not one this run's records handed out
  carries: ReadRecords
    refuses 400 "not a cursor of this run's records"
      why: a page of records resumes from the cursor the page before it returned, so any other text is a mistake the caller made

ARunsLife
A workflow starts on a branch, moves through two nodes, stops to ask the operator,
    carries on after the answer, and ends with a failure. At every stage the fleet and
    the run's page say where it is.
ARunBlockedOnTwoGates\nA run asks two questions at once, the later path first. The page lists the gates by\n    path, a second ask at a path replaces its question, and an exit clears them all.

TheFleetIsOrdered
Three runs report in the order finished, running, blocked. The fleet puts the blocked
    one first, then the running one, then the finished one, and the attention list names
    the blocked and the ended run.
FindingARun\nTwo runs are on the fleet. Typing one's name keeps that run and drops the other, and a\n    name no run has keeps neither.
TheAttendantIsSwitched\nThe operator turns the attendant on, sees the fleet report it, turns it off again, and\n    sees the switch back where it began.

UnknownRuns
A push that names no run is ignored, a gate needs a path as well, and asking for a run
    nobody pushed gets a page that says it was not found. A run that exits before it ever
    reported still lands on the fleet, shown by its id.

ReadingARun
An operator opens a run that waits on a gate. They read the gate, try to answer it and are told
    the run's workspace cannot be reached, leave the run a message and an empty one, and look at its
    cost, its turns, its records, its transcripts and its files. A run that never reported has
    nothing to show, and its stored telemetry is empty, not missing.

NothingIsArchived
An operator looks for a finished run in the archive and in the history. groom has archived
    nothing, so each archive read says no run is archived under that id, the history lists no
    ended run of ours, and asking to read a summary again changes nothing.

TheOperatorTendsGroom
An operator checks what groom holds besides the fleet. No run is live, no checkout is
    listed, the attendant has nothing waiting and no log, no dispatch queue is configured, and a
    rescan and a reload find nothing to do. Turning the attendant on changes only its mode.
- **(none)**: the fleet holds no run of ours. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **running**: the run reported progress and holds no gate. Reached by: POST /push/progress {"container_id": "r00", "name": "r00", "current_node": "build"}.
- **blocked**: the run waits on one gate. Reached by: POST /push/blocked {"container_id": "r01", "file_path": "gates/approve.md", "question": "Ship it?", "name": "r01"}.
- **finished**: the run exited with a code. Reached by: POST /push/exited {"container_id": "r02", "exit_code": 2, "name": "r02"}.
- **serving**: groom answers and holds nothing the book did not push. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **Off**: no attendant answers the gates. Reached by: a fresh service, nothing done.
- **Headless**: an attendant answers the gates. Reached by: POST /api/settings/attend {"enabled": true}.
